name: Spare OS
replaces: Paying for Microsoft Windows (Home, Pro, Enterprise and Education), the Windows device-management and server licences offices and schools buy with it, and the paid utilities people add on top
summary: A free Linux-based operating system for ordinary PCs and laptops, with every Spare app built in, a one-step move from Windows and updates that can't leave a machine broken. Offices, schools and co-ops can run and manage many machines without paid licences.

areas.name: Base system and hardware
areas.summary: The proven Linux base, the build line that turns it into signed Spare OS images, and the work that makes it run well on ordinary and old PCs.

features.name: Run on a proven Linux base
features.does: Use a stable, well-supported Linux system underneath, without the co-op writing or maintaining a kernel.

parts.name: Base distribution decision
parts.what: Compare Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu, NixOS and others on stability, hardware support, update model and support length, and pick one.

parts.name: System image build line
parts.what: Builds every Spare OS image from a declared recipe on the kit's release pipeline, so each release is the same on every machine.

parts.name: Image recipe and package list
parts.what: The public, versioned list of every package, setting and default that goes into an image.

parts.name: Reproducible build checks
parts.what: Rebuilds each release independently and compares the result, following the kit's reproducible build rules, so anyone can check an image matches its source.

parts.name: Signing keys and key ceremony
parts.what: Keeps the keys that sign images, packages and boot files offline under the kit's two-person key control, with a written, witnessed process for using and replacing them.

parts.name: Upstream first
parts.what: Sends our fixes, drivers and translations, including te reo Māori, to the open projects Spare OS ships, and keeps a short public list of the patches we still carry.

features.name: Work on ordinary and old PCs
features.does: Install on most PCs and laptops from the last 15 years, including ones Windows 11 refuses to run on.

parts.name: Hardware support targets
parts.what: Sets the minimum processor, memory and disk, with no TPM or new-processor requirement, and checks it against common old PCs.

parts.name: Kernel track
parts.what: Chooses which Linux kernel series each release follows, balancing new hardware support against stability.

parts.name: Light mode for old machines
parts.what: A lighter desktop profile with fewer effects and background services for PCs with 4 GB of memory or less.

parts.name: Hardware test lab
parts.what: A pool of real PCs, laptops, printers and docks, many donated by members, that every release is tested on.

parts.name: Hardware compatibility list
parts.what: A public, searchable list of PC models and devices with how well each works, built from the lab and members' reports.

parts.name: Old start-up modes decision
parts.what: Decides whether to support PCs that start in legacy BIOS mode or have Windows on an MBR disk, as many 2011 to 2013 PCs do and dual boot then needs, and how that fits signed start-up and image updates.

parts.name: Wipe standard for donated PCs
parts.what: A written standard for wiping every donated PC before it enters the test lab or the refurbishment programme, with a record of each wipe, because donors' personal data on those disks stays the co-op's responsibility under the Privacy Act.

features.name: Get drivers without hunting
features.does: Have devices work straight away, and install any extra driver a device needs with one click.

parts.name: Driver detection and offers
parts.what: Spots devices that need an extra driver or firmware file and offers the right one from the store.

parts.name: Graphics drivers
parts.what: Ships or offers graphics drivers, including NVIDIA's, signed so they load with Secure Boot on, following the policy for software that is not open source.

parts.name: Firmware files package
parts.what: Packages the firmware files Wi-Fi cards, Bluetooth and graphics chips need, keeping each maker's redistribution terms and following the policy for software that is not open source.

parts.name: Missing-driver report
parts.what: Tells the person which device has no driver, what that means, and with their consent reports it so the co-op can chase it.

parts.name: Laptops with two graphics chips
parts.what: Picks the graphics chip for each app, uses the power-saving chip by default, and is tested on the lab's work and gaming laptops.

features.name: Update device firmware
features.does: Update the PC's start-up firmware and device firmware from inside Spare OS, including Secure Boot certificate and revocation updates.

parts.name: Firmware update service link
parts.what: Uses the open firmware update service that PC makers publish to, checking each update's signature, and is how a PC with Windows removed gets new Secure Boot certificates and revocation lists.

parts.name: Firmware updates screen
parts.what: Shows available firmware updates in plain words, with a warning to keep the laptop plugged in.

features.name: Get good battery life and sleep
features.does: Close the lid and open it again with everything working, and get battery life close to what Windows gives.

parts.name: Power profiles
parts.what: Balanced, quiet and performance modes that adjust the processor, screen and background work.

parts.name: Sleep and wake testing
parts.what: Tests sleep, hibernate and wake on the lab's laptops each release and records which models have problems.

parts.name: Battery health and charge limit
parts.what: Shows battery wear and lets people cap charging at 80% on laptops that support it.

parts.name: Hibernation with signed start-up and encryption
parts.what: Decides how hibernation works with Secure Boot and full-disk encryption, since the kernel lockdown that signed start-up turns on blocks hibernation unless the saved memory image is protected, and offers hibernate only where it works.

features.name: Run on ARM laptops and small boards
features.does: Use Spare OS on ARM laptops and Raspberry Pi-class computers as well as ordinary PCs.

parts.name: ARM support research
parts.what: Checks which ARM laptops and boards have enough open driver support to be worth a release.

parts.name: ARM image builds
parts.what: Adds ARM images to the build line once a target is chosen.

areas.name: Get, try and install
areas.summary: Every way a person gets Spare OS onto a PC: downloading it, making a USB stick or getting one ready-made, trying it without changes, installing beside or instead of Windows, installing many PCs at once, buying a PC with it already on, and later old Macs and Chromebooks, all usable with a screen reader from the first screen.

features.name: Download Spare OS
features.does: Download Spare OS free from the website, with a simple check that the file has not been tampered with.

parts.name: Download website
parts.what: A plain page that picks the right image for the person's PC and explains each step in short sentences.

parts.name: Mirrors and peer-to-peer downloads
parts.what: A network of download mirrors, including member-run ones, plus torrent downloads, all checked against signed update metadata, with costs shown on the ledger.

parts.name: Signature check
parts.what: Checks the downloaded image's signature automatically in the USB maker, and explains how to check it by hand.

features.name: Make a USB stick from Windows
features.does: Turn a USB stick into a Spare OS installer from a Windows PC with one small program.

parts.name: USB maker for Windows
parts.what: Our own small, open program that downloads the image, checks it and writes it to a USB stick.

parts.name: USB maker for Mac and Linux
parts.what: The same USB maker built for macOS and Linux.

parts.name: Boot menu help
parts.what: A list by PC maker of the key that opens the boot menu, plus how to turn off Windows fast start-up first.

parts.name: Signed Windows and Mac builds
parts.what: Signs the USB maker and Windows-side helper with a co-op Authenticode certificate (Microsoft's Artifact Signing issues them to NZ organisations) and Mac builds with Apple Developer ID notarisation, through the kit's signed releases and held by the legal entity with costs on the ledger, so SmartScreen and Smart App Control let them run; the certificates belong in the kit for every Spare desktop app.

parts.name: Accessible, translated Windows tools
parts.what: Makes the USB maker and the Windows-side helper work fully with Windows screen readers, the keyboard alone and high contrast, and translates them, since they are the first Spare programs a blind person runs.

features.name: Try it without installing
features.does: Start Spare OS from the USB stick and check Wi-Fi, sound, screen and printer before changing anything on the PC.

parts.name: Live session
parts.what: A full Spare OS session that runs from the USB stick and leaves the PC's disk untouched.

parts.name: Hardware check report
parts.what: Shows which devices work and which need attention, and with consent adds the result to the compatibility list.

parts.name: Accessibility and language before install
parts.what: Screen reader, zoom, high contrast and language choice can be turned on from the first screen of the USB session and stay on through the installer.

features.name: Install beside Windows or instead of it
features.does: Install Spare OS next to Windows, choosing at start-up, or replace Windows completely, without losing files.

parts.name: Installer framework decision
parts.what: Compares existing open installers on safety, disk handling and how easily they can be made simple.

parts.name: Installer app
parts.what: Guides the person through install in a few screens, with safe defaults and a clear summary before anything changes.

parts.name: Safe Windows partition shrinking
parts.what: Shrinks the Windows partition from inside Windows through the Windows-side helper, because a BitLocker volume cannot be resized from Linux, or from the installer only when BitLocker is off, after making sure the person has the recovery key; Windows 11 turns device encryption on by default on many PCs.

parts.name: Start-up chooser
parts.what: Adds Spare OS and Windows to a start-up menu that picks the last used system by default.

parts.name: Encryption at install
parts.what: Turns on full-disk encryption during install by default, with the recovery key shown and saved.

parts.name: Install failure recovery
parts.what: If install stops part way, leaves Windows untouched and saves a log the person can send for help.

parts.name: Accessible start-up menu
parts.what: The start-up menu plays a sound when it appears, can speak or sound out each choice, uses large clear text, and offers a choice that starts with the screen reader on.

parts.name: Hidden disk check
parts.what: Spots Intel RST or VMD storage modes that hide the disk from the installer, and explains the fix in plain steps that keep Windows starting.

features.name: Install many PCs at once
features.does: Install Spare OS on a room full of PCs over the network or from an answer file, without clicking through each one.

parts.name: Answer file format
parts.what: A documented file that answers every installer question in advance.

parts.name: Network install
parts.what: Starts install over the office or school network, pulling the image from a local server.

parts.name: Factory install mode
parts.what: Installs now and leaves language, account and Wi-Fi for the new owner's first start, for PC sellers and refurbishers.

features.name: Buy a PC with Spare OS on it
features.does: Buy a new or refurbished PC with Spare OS already installed and supported.

parts.name: PC maker partnership terms
parts.what: The agreement a PC maker or refurbisher signs to sell PCs with Spare OS, covering support and naming.

parts.name: Refurbished PC programme
parts.what: How local repairers take old Windows 10 PCs, wipe them to the written standard, refurbish them with Spare OS and sell them on at a fair price.

parts.name: Works with Spare OS badge
parts.what: A badge for hardware that passes the lab's tests, listed on the compatibility list.

parts.name: Pre-installed image and recovery
parts.what: The factory image partners install, with a recovery option that returns the PC to as-new using the same reset as the system's own repair tools.

features.name: Get Spare OS without making a USB stick
features.does: Get a ready-made Spare OS stick at cost, borrow one from a library or helper, or start the installer from Windows.

parts.name: Ready-made sticks and loans
parts.what: Ready-made Spare OS sticks sold at cost, and loan sticks held by libraries and member helpers, with costs on the ledger.

parts.name: Start the installer from Windows
parts.what: Researches starting the Spare OS installer straight from Windows without a USB stick, and how that stays safe with BitLocker and Secure Boot.

features.name: Put Spare OS on an old Mac or Chromebook
features.does: Install Spare OS on an Intel Mac that no longer gets macOS updates, or a school Chromebook past its update end date.

parts.name: Old Intel Macs
parts.what: Checks which Intel Macs that no longer get macOS updates run Spare OS well, including start-up, Wi-Fi, keyboards and the security chip on later models.

parts.name: Chromebooks past their update date
parts.what: Checks how school Chromebooks past their update end date can start Spare OS, what firmware change each needs and the risk of each step, before offering it.

areas.name: First start
areas.summary: The first few minutes after install or on a new PC: language, keyboard, Wi-Fi, an account, privacy choices and a short welcome, all usable by everyone from the first screen.

features.name: Set up in a few minutes
features.does: Choose language, keyboard, time zone, Wi-Fi and a name in a few plain steps.

parts.name: First-start setup app
parts.what: The step-by-step screens that run on first start, each with a clear back button and skip where it is safe.

parts.name: Time zone and region guess
parts.what: Suggests time zone and regional formats from the chosen language and keyboard, with an optional online check through the private location lookup.

parts.name: Accessibility from the first screen
parts.what: Screen reader, magnifier and high contrast can be turned on from the very first screen with a keyboard shortcut or by voice, carrying on any choices made in the USB session.

features.name: Make an account without going online
features.does: Create a local account on the PC with no internet and no online login required.

parts.name: Local account creation
parts.what: Makes the first user an administrator with a password or PIN, entirely on the device.

parts.name: Age range at each account's set-up
parts.what: Asks the age range at the set-up of every account on the PC where the law requires it, not only the first user's, stores only the range and keeps it on the device.

features.name: Connect a Spareware login
features.does: Optionally connect a Spareware login so Spare apps, files and chosen settings follow the person to any PC.

parts.name: Spareware login at setup
parts.what: Signs in with a passkey or password through the accounts service, and links it to the local account.

parts.name: Settings sync choice
parts.what: Lets the person choose which settings sync between their PCs, all off until they turn them on, with Wi-Fi passwords and other secrets left out until end-to-end encrypted sync (OS-A12-F11) is ready.

features.name: Make clear privacy choices
features.does: See every data-sharing option in plain words and choose, with all sharing off by default.

parts.name: Privacy choices screen
parts.what: One screen listing each choice, what is sent, to whom and why, with nothing pre-ticked.

parts.name: Spare OS privacy notice
parts.what: Adds what Spare OS itself collects, in plain words, to the kit's collection notices, checked against privacy law in NZ and the main overseas markets.

features.name: Take a short welcome tour
features.does: Learn where things are, especially for someone coming from Windows.

parts.name: Welcome tour
parts.what: A short, skippable tour of the start menu, files, settings, store and help.

parts.name: Where did it go guide
parts.what: A searchable list that maps common Windows tasks and places to where they are in Spare OS.

features.name: Pick a layout
features.does: Choose a desktop layout that suits them: a familiar taskbar layout, a dock layout, or a simple large-button layout.

parts.name: Layout presets
parts.what: Our own designed layouts built on the desktop's settings, with no copied visuals from other systems.

features.name: Restore from another PC or backup
features.does: Start a new PC by restoring files, apps and settings from a backup or another Spare OS PC.

parts.name: Restore during setup
parts.what: Offers restore from a backup drive, Spareware storage or a nearby PC as one of the first-start steps.

areas.name: Moving from Windows
areas.summary: The guided move: files, browser data, email, Wi-Fi and personal settings brought across, a report of which programs have replacements, and Windows kept alongside until the person is ready.

features.name: Bring my files across
features.does: Copy Documents, Pictures, Desktop, Music and Videos from Windows on the same PC, another PC or a backup drive.

parts.name: Move-across design
parts.what: Decides what is brought across and how, and how Windows is kept alongside.

parts.name: Windows folder reader
parts.what: Finds each Windows user's folders on an NTFS partition or drive and reads them safely without changing them.

parts.name: Move-across app
parts.what: One guided app that shows what was found, lets the person tick what to bring, copies it and reports what moved.

parts.name: PC-to-PC transfer
parts.what: Moves files and settings from an old PC to a new one over the local network or a cable.

parts.name: Cloud-only files check
parts.what: Spots files that only exist as cloud placeholders on Windows and helps the person download them before the move.

features.name: Bring my browser across
features.does: Bring bookmarks, history and saved passwords from Edge, Chrome or Firefox into the Spare OS browser.

parts.name: Browser profile importer
parts.what: Imports bookmarks and history from browser profile files, and passwords only through the browser's own export, never by breaking its encryption.

features.name: Bring my email, contacts and calendars
features.does: Keep using the same email accounts, contacts and calendars without setting them up again.

parts.name: Account finder
parts.what: Lists the email, calendar and contact accounts the person used on Windows so they can sign in to them again in one place.

parts.name: Outlook data file import
parts.what: Reads Outlook data files from Microsoft's published file format specification and imports mail, contacts and calendars; the reader belongs in the kit or an engine so Spare Office's importer uses the same one.

features.name: Bring my Wi-Fi and network settings
features.does: Connect to known Wi-Fi networks, printers and network drives straight away after the move.

parts.name: Wi-Fi and printer import
parts.what: Imports Wi-Fi networks, printers and mapped network drives from the Windows-side helper's bundle.

parts.name: Windows-side helper
parts.what: A small open program the person runs on Windows before moving, which packs up settings, Wi-Fi networks, printers and the program list using Windows' own export tools.

features.name: Find replacements for my programs
features.does: See each Windows program they had, and whether it runs on Spare OS, has a Spare app replacement, or has an open alternative.

parts.name: Installed program scan
parts.what: Reads the list of installed programs from the helper's bundle or the Windows partition.

parts.name: Program equivalents list
parts.what: Open data mapping common Windows programs to Spare apps, open alternatives, or how well they run in the compatibility layer.

parts.name: Replacement report
parts.what: A plain report: ready to use, will run, needs a replacement, or blocks switching for now, with links to install each.

parts.name: Paid licence warning
parts.what: Warns the person to deactivate paid programs such as design, accounting and office software, and to save their product keys, before Windows is removed, since many licences limit activations.

features.name: Bring my look and preferences
features.does: Keep wallpaper, mouse and keyboard settings, region formats and default printer as they were.

parts.name: Settings translator
parts.what: Turns Windows settings from the helper's bundle into the matching Spare OS settings, and lists any it cannot match.

features.name: Keep Windows alongside, then remove it
features.does: Keep Windows to start into while getting used to Spare OS, then safely reclaim its space later.

parts.name: Dual start manager
parts.what: The settings page for the start-up chooser, where the person picks the default system and how long the menu waits.

parts.name: Reclaim Windows space
parts.what: Checks nothing unmoved remains and paid licences are released, offers a backup, then removes Windows and grows Spare OS into the space.

parts.name: Watch for Windows boot blocks
parts.what: Tests each Windows update that changes Secure Boot rules on the lab's dual-boot PCs, as Microsoft's August 2024 SBAT update did when it stopped many Linux systems starting, and ships fixes before members are hit.

features.name: Open Windows drives and files
features.does: Open NTFS and exFAT drives, BitLocker-locked drives with the key, and Windows shortcuts and file types.

parts.name: NTFS and exFAT read and write
parts.what: Uses the kernel's open NTFS and exFAT support so Windows drives open like any other.

parts.name: BitLocker drive unlock
parts.what: Unlocks BitLocker drives with the person's password or recovery key through an existing open tool shipped as a separate program, once an owner has cleared it.

features.name: Move with help from a person
features.does: Book a trained member helper to do the move with them, in person or remotely.

parts.name: Helper booking
parts.what: Links the move-across app to the member support network, so the helper sees only what the person shares.

areas.name: Desktop and windows
areas.summary: The desktop a person sees every day: taskbar, start menu, search, window arranging, notifications, quick settings, screenshots, themes, sounds, touch screens, the touchpad and the lock screen. It should feel familiar to Windows users while being our own design.

features.name: Use a familiar desktop
features.does: Find a taskbar, start menu, tray and clock where a Windows user expects them, from the first minute.

parts.name: Desktop decision
parts.what: Compare KDE Plasma, GNOME and others on how familiar they can be made, stability and accessibility, and pick one.

parts.name: Spare OS layout and theme
parts.what: Our own default layout, colours and visual style following the Spareware design guide, set up on the chosen desktop.

parts.name: Spare OS icon set
parts.what: Our own icons for apps, files and the system, drawn from scratch with no copied artwork.

parts.name: Default fonts
parts.what: Sets open interface fonts, and installs engine-text's shared metric-matched fonts system-wide so documents keep their layout.

parts.name: Spare OS sounds and pointers
parts.what: Our own system sounds and pointer set, made from scratch with no copied sounds or artwork.

features.name: Find anything from the start menu
features.does: Type in one box to find apps, files, settings, quick sums and answers.

parts.name: Desktop search service
parts.what: Searches apps, settings, files and commands as the person types, from a local index.

parts.name: Search results panel
parts.what: Shows grouped results in the start menu with keyboard control and clear actions.

features.name: Arrange windows
features.does: Snap windows to halves, quarters and grids, maximise, minimise and switch between them by keyboard or mouse.

parts.name: Window snapping layouts
parts.what: Drag-to-edge and keyboard snapping into simple layouts, remembered per screen.

parts.name: Window switcher
parts.what: Switch between open windows with a keyboard shortcut and a clear preview.

parts.name: Familiar keyboard shortcuts
parts.what: The shortcuts Windows users already know for common actions, set as defaults and listed in help.

features.name: Use several desktops and screens
features.does: Work across virtual desktops and several monitors, each with its own scaling.

parts.name: Virtual desktops
parts.what: Create, switch and move windows between desktops.

parts.name: Several monitors and mixed scaling
parts.what: Remembers each monitor's layout and sharpness setting, and moves windows back when a screen is unplugged.

features.name: See and act on notifications
features.does: See notifications in one place, reply or act from them, and silence them while working.

parts.name: Notification centre
parts.what: Lists notifications by app with actions, and keeps a short history.

parts.name: Spare app notifications link
parts.what: Delivers notifications from Spare apps and the messaging service to the desktop, respecting each person's choices.

parts.name: Focus and do not disturb
parts.what: Quiet hours and focus sessions that hold back notifications except chosen ones.

features.name: Change common settings quickly
features.does: Turn Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, volume, brightness and power mode up or down from one small panel.

parts.name: Quick settings panel
parts.what: A panel from the tray with the most used switches and sliders.

features.name: Copy and paste with history
features.does: Paste from recent copies, and insert emoji and special characters.

parts.name: Clipboard history
parts.what: Keeps recent copies on the device only, skips password fields, and can be cleared or turned off.

parts.name: Emoji and symbol picker
parts.what: A keyboard shortcut that opens emoji, symbols and macron letters to insert anywhere.

features.name: Take screenshots and record the screen
features.does: Capture the whole screen, a window or an area, mark it up, and record the screen as video.

parts.name: Screenshot tool
parts.what: Captures, marks up with arrows, text and blur, and copies or saves.

parts.name: Screen recorder
parts.what: Records the screen or a window with sound to a common video format.

parts.name: Copy text from the screen
parts.what: Picks text out of a screenshot or image so it can be copied.

features.name: Make it look my way
features.does: Choose dark or light mode, accent colour, wallpaper, text size and night light.

parts.name: Themes and dark mode
parts.what: Light, dark and high-contrast themes that every built-in app follows.

parts.name: Wallpaper collection
parts.what: Wallpapers made and given by members and photographers, each with its licence and credit.

parts.name: Night light
parts.what: Warms the screen colour in the evening on a schedule.

features.name: Use touch screens and the on-screen keyboard
features.does: Use a touch laptop or tablet with gestures and an on-screen keyboard.

parts.name: Touch gestures and tablet layout
parts.what: Larger targets and swipe gestures when a keyboard is folded away or detached.

parts.name: On-screen keyboard
parts.what: A full on-screen keyboard that appears in text boxes on touch screens, with every installed layout.

features.name: Lock the screen and switch users
features.does: Lock the PC, sign back in, and let another person sign in without closing the first person's work.

parts.name: Lock and sign-in screen
parts.what: The sign-in and lock screens, with user switching and accessibility options visible.

features.name: Glance at widgets
features.does: Glance at weather, calendar and chosen news, with no ads and only from sources the person picks.

parts.name: Widgets panel
parts.what: A panel of small cards the person chooses, drawn from local apps and open data.

parts.name: Open weather and news sources
parts.what: Finds weather and news sources whose terms allow use, starting with New Zealand ones.

features.name: Use the touchpad
features.does: Scroll, swipe between desktops and apps, and change touchpad settings such as tap to click and speed.

parts.name: Touchpad gestures and settings
parts.what: Two- and three-finger gestures for scrolling and switching desktops and apps, plus settings for tapping, speed, palm rejection and turning the touchpad off while typing.

areas.name: Settings and system tools
areas.summary: One place to change every setting, plus the everyday system tools: seeing what's running, freeing space, default apps, system information, devices and logs, disks, the command line, and tools for developers.

features.name: Change any setting in one place
features.does: Find and change every setting in one settings app, searching in plain words.

parts.name: Settings app
parts.what: One app with every setting grouped by plain-word topic, where each change is a system command that can be undone.

parts.name: Settings search
parts.what: Finds settings from everyday words, including the names Windows uses for them.

features.name: See what's running and stop it
features.does: See which apps use the processor, memory, disk and network, end a stuck app, and choose what starts with the PC.

parts.name: Task manager
parts.what: Lists apps and background services with their use of the processor, memory, disk, network and battery, and ends them safely.

parts.name: Start-up apps control
parts.what: Lists everything that starts automatically and lets the person turn each off.

features.name: Free up disk space
features.does: See what fills the disk and clear caches, old system versions and leftovers safely.

parts.name: Storage overview and clean-up
parts.what: Shows space by type and offers safe clean-ups, never deleting the person's own files without asking.

features.name: Choose default apps
features.does: Pick which app opens each kind of file and link.

parts.name: Default apps and file links
parts.what: Stores defaults per file type and link type, and asks once when a new app could take over.

features.name: See system information
features.does: See the PC model, parts, Spare OS version and support end date, and copy them for a help request.

parts.name: About this PC
parts.what: One page with model, processor, memory, graphics, storage, version and support dates.

parts.name: Copyable system report
parts.what: A text report of the PC's set-up that the person can read before sharing for help.

features.name: Set date, time and power buttons
features.does: Keep the clock right, and choose what the power button and lid do.

parts.name: Date, time and network time
parts.what: Sets the clock automatically from network time servers, with time zone changes for travel.

parts.name: Power button and lid settings
parts.what: Chooses sleep, hibernate, shut down or nothing for the power button and lid, offering hibernate only where it works with encryption and signed start-up.

features.name: Manage disks
features.does: Format, partition, check the health of and mount drives.

parts.name: Disk utility
parts.what: Formats, partitions, encrypts and checks drives, with plain warnings before anything is erased.

parts.name: Drive health warnings
parts.what: Reads drive health data and warns early when a drive looks likely to fail.

features.name: Use a command line
features.does: Open a terminal and run any system action as a typed command.

parts.name: Terminal app
parts.what: A tabbed terminal for power users and for following help guides.

parts.name: Spare command-line tool
parts.what: One command-line tool that runs every system command, with help text for each.

features.name: Run virtual machines and developer tools
features.does: Run virtual machines and containers, and set up programming tools in one click.

parts.name: Virtual machine manager
parts.what: Creates and runs virtual machines from an open virtualisation stack with a simple interface.

parts.name: Container tools
parts.what: Open container tools set up so developers can run containers without extra steps.

parts.name: Developer set-up packs
parts.what: One-click packs that install common programming languages and tools from the store.

features.name: See devices and system logs
features.does: See every device with its driver and whether it works, turn a device off, and read the system log when helping someone.

parts.name: Devices page
parts.what: Lists each device, its driver and whether it works, links to the missing-driver report, and can turn a device off.

parts.name: System log viewer
parts.what: Shows system logs in plain words with filters by time, app and severity, for helpers and IT staff.

areas.name: Files and storage
areas.summary: Finding, opening and managing files: the file manager, archives, fast search, network folders, Spareware storage and other clouds, USB drives and phones, earlier versions and tags.

features.name: Browse and manage files
features.does: Browse, copy, move, rename and delete files in a file manager with tabs, previews and a recycle bin.

parts.name: File manager
parts.what: A file manager with tabs, a side bar of places, list and grid views, and copy progress that can be paused.

parts.name: Thumbnails and previews
parts.what: Shows thumbnails and quick previews of pictures, video, PDFs and office files.

parts.name: Recycle bin with restore
parts.what: Deleted files go to a bin first and can be put back where they came from.

features.name: Open zip and other archives
features.does: Open, make and extract zip, 7z, tar and other archive files from the file manager.

parts.name: Archive support
parts.what: Open archive tools wired into the file manager's right-click menu.

features.name: Find files fast
features.does: Find any file by name or by words inside it within a second.

parts.name: File index
parts.what: A local index of file names and contents that runs when the PC is idle, skips private folders the person picks, and never leaves the device.

parts.name: Content readers
parts.what: Pull text out of documents, PDFs and other common formats for the index.

features.name: Use shared and network folders
features.does: Open office and home network folders and drives, and share a folder with others on the network.

parts.name: Network folders
parts.what: Opens Windows-style network shares and home network drives, and remembers them as mapped places.

parts.name: Share a folder
parts.what: Shares a folder on the local network from its right-click menu with simple permissions.

features.name: Keep files in Spareware storage
features.does: Keep chosen folders in the person's Spareware storage, synced across PCs, with files downloaded only when opened.

parts.name: Desktop sync client
parts.what: Syncs chosen folders with the person's Spareware storage on the kit, handling conflicts and offline changes; one client for every Spare program, so it belongs in the kit and Spare OS never depends on Spare Office's drive.

parts.name: Files on demand
parts.what: Shows every cloud file but downloads it only when opened, and frees space for files not used lately, as part of the same shared sync client.

parts.name: Other cloud accounts
parts.what: Connects other storage over open protocols, and other providers through their published interfaces where terms allow.

features.name: Use USB drives, phones and cameras
features.does: Plug in a USB drive, phone or camera and see its files, and remove it safely.

parts.name: Removable drives
parts.what: Opens new drives, warns before unplugging during a copy, and handles common drive formats.

parts.name: Photo import from phones and cameras
parts.what: Imports photos and videos from phones and cameras plugged in by USB into dated folders, skipping ones already imported, with no phone link needed.

features.name: Get back an earlier version of a file
features.does: Restore an earlier version of a file or a deleted folder from automatic snapshots.

parts.name: File version history
parts.what: Takes automatic local snapshots of the person's folders and shows earlier versions from the right-click menu, so files come back after a mistake or ransomware.

features.name: Tag and organise files
features.does: Add tags and favourites, and see recently used files in every app's open dialog.

parts.name: Tags and favourites
parts.what: Stores tags with the files and shows them in the file manager and search.

areas.name: Built-in apps
areas.summary: What is on the PC from the first start: every Spare app with one login, a private web browser that warns about scam sites, the small everyday apps, media, mail and contacts shared by all apps, maps, meetings, fonts and disc burning.

features.name: Use every Spare app straight away
features.does: Open Spare Office, Spare Studio, Spare Construct, Spare Social and the marketplace apps from the start menu, already signed in.

parts.name: Spare apps bundle
parts.what: Decides which Spare apps ship in the image and which are one click away in the store, keeping the download size sensible.

parts.name: One login for all Spare apps
parts.what: Shares the Spareware login from the system with every Spare app, so the person signs in once.

parts.name: Spare apps on the system update channel
parts.what: Updates Spare apps through the same channel and schedule as the system.

parts.name: Desktop entries for web-based Spare apps
parts.what: Gives the marketplace apps that run in a browser their own start menu entries, windows and notifications.

features.name: Browse the web
features.does: Use a fast, private web browser that keeps up with security fixes.

parts.name: Browser choice
parts.what: Compares the main open browsers on security update speed, privacy, licence and website compatibility, and picks a default.

parts.name: Browser defaults
parts.what: Sets private defaults with no paid search placement, and documents every default and why.

parts.name: Phishing and scam site warnings
parts.what: Warns before phishing and scam websites using a block list checked privately on the device, and spots fake 'your PC is infected' pages, so people new to Spare OS are protected as they were on Windows.

features.name: Use the small everyday apps
features.does: Use a text editor, calculator, clocks and alarms, image viewer, PDF viewer, camera and sound recorder.

parts.name: Small apps set
parts.what: Chooses mature open apps for each everyday job and fits them to the Spare OS look.

parts.name: PDF viewer and form filler
parts.what: Opens, searches, fills and signs PDF forms.

parts.name: Camera app
parts.what: Takes photos and video from the built-in or USB camera.

features.name: Play music and video
features.does: Play common music and video files, and discs where the law allows it.

parts.name: Media player
parts.what: A media player for local files and playlists that handles every codec Spare OS can legally ship.

features.name: Make quick photo edits
features.does: Crop, rotate, straighten and adjust photos, and draw simple pictures, without opening a big app.

parts.name: Quick photo editor
parts.what: Simple edits in the image viewer, handing off to Spare Studio for anything bigger.

features.name: Share contacts, calendars and accounts across apps
features.does: Add mail, calendar and contact accounts once and have every app use them.

parts.name: System contacts and calendar store
parts.what: One local store for contacts and calendars that syncs over open protocols and any app can read with permission.

parts.name: Online accounts panel
parts.what: Adds email, calendar, contact and storage accounts once in settings for every app to use.

features.name: See maps and directions
features.does: Search places and get directions on open map data.

parts.name: Maps app
parts.what: A maps app on the shared maps service, with offline maps for chosen regions.

features.name: Join video calls and share the screen
features.does: Join calls in Spare apps or any other service's web or desktop app, with camera, microphone and screen sharing working.

parts.name: Call readiness
parts.what: Makes camera, microphone, echo control and screen sharing work in browsers and call apps through the system's sharing permissions.

features.name: Install fonts and burn discs
features.does: Install a font by double-clicking it, and burn files, music or photos to CDs and DVDs on PCs that have a drive.

parts.name: Font installer
parts.what: Previews a font file and installs it for one user or the whole PC by double-click, and removes it again from settings.

parts.name: Disc burning
parts.what: Burns data, music and photo discs from the file manager with an open burning tool, for older PCs that still have a drive.

areas.name: App store
areas.summary: Installing, updating and removing software from one trusted store or other sources the person adds: permissions shown up front, verified makers, ratings, reports, age ratings, payments, refunds and tips at cost, the maker's side of publishing, plugins, web apps, parental approval and offline installs.

features.name: Install apps from the store or elsewhere
features.does: Browse, search, install, update and remove apps from one store, and still add other open app sources or install a maker's own app file.

parts.name: Store app
parts.what: Browse by category, search, see screenshots and details, install, update and remove.

parts.name: App packaging format decision
parts.what: Compares sandboxed app formats on security, size, update speed and how many apps already use them, and picks one.

parts.name: App catalogue service
parts.what: Holds the list of apps, their versions and checks, drawing on existing open app collections plus Spare apps.

parts.name: Other app sources and app files
parts.what: Lets the person add other open app sources and install app files from a maker's website, with a clear warning about who checked them and the same sandbox as store apps.

features.name: Know what an app can reach
features.does: See what an app can reach (files, camera, microphone, location, network) before installing, and change it later.

parts.name: Permissions view
parts.what: Shows an app's permissions in plain words before install and in settings afterwards, with switches to change them.

features.name: Trust who made an app
features.does: See whether an app comes from its real maker, read ratings and reviews, and report a harmful app.

parts.name: Maker verification
parts.what: Checks that an app's publisher really controls the project, and shows a mark when they do.

parts.name: Ratings and reviews
parts.what: Ratings and reviews from people who installed the app, never from agents, with the trust service's tools against fakes.

parts.name: Report and takedown
parts.what: Lets anyone report a harmful app; decisions and removals go in the public log with the rule behind them.

parts.name: Submission checks
parts.what: Automated malware and policy checks on every new app version before it is listed, sharing its scanners with the kit's plugin review once that is ready.

features.name: Pay for or tip app makers
features.does: Buy paid apps or tip open-source makers, with the at-cost fee shown and the rest going to the maker.

parts.name: App payments
parts.what: Takes payments and tips through the regulated payment provider, with the at-cost fee on the ledger.

parts.name: Tax on digital sales
parts.what: Works out and collects GST, VAT and sales tax on app sales where the store must, on the kit's GST engine, starting with NZ.

parts.name: Refunds and consumer guarantees for apps
parts.what: Refunds for app purchases on the kit's refunds service, following NZ consumer guarantees for digital content and the EU's digital content rules.

parts.name: Receipts and tax invoices for apps
parts.what: Gives every app purchase a receipt, and a tax invoice where the law needs one, through the kit.

parts.name: App subscriptions
parts.what: Lets makers sell subscriptions that the person can see and cancel in one place, on the kit's regular payments.

features.name: Add plugins and AI tools
features.does: Find and install plugins for Spare apps and AI tools that connect through MCP, with the same permissions view.

parts.name: Plugin and MCP tool listings
parts.what: Lists sandboxed plugins and MCP tools in the store with their declared permissions, after the kit's plugin review and signing.

features.name: Install a website as an app
features.does: Install a website as an app with its own window, icon and notifications.

parts.name: Web app install
parts.what: Turns a site into an app from the browser or the store, in its own window.

features.name: Ask a parent before installing or buying
features.does: Let a child ask to install or buy an app, and a parent approve or decline from their own account, with spending limits and age ratings to guide them.

parts.name: Install approvals
parts.what: Holds a child's install request until a parent approves, using the age range and family settings.

parts.name: Purchase approvals and spending limits
parts.what: Holds a child's purchase until a parent approves and sets spending limits per child, meeting app store laws that need parent consent for purchases as well as downloads, such as Texas's, which courts let take effect in 2026.

parts.name: Age ratings for apps and games
parts.what: Gives every app and game an age rating from an open, questionnaire-based rating scheme, shown in the store and used by family settings.

parts.name: Game classification law
parts.what: Checks NZ classification law for games sold through the store, and overseas equivalents, and how ratings and labels must be shown.

features.name: Install apps without good internet
features.does: Install and update apps from a local cache or a USB drive, for schools and places with poor internet.

parts.name: Offline app bundles and local cache
parts.what: Copies apps and updates once to a local server or drive and installs from there.

features.name: Publish an app
features.does: As an app maker, sign up, agree the maker terms, upload and sign versions, follow review, appeal a rejection, see sales and get paid.

parts.name: Maker account and agreement
parts.what: A maker account and a plain-words maker agreement covering listing rules, fees at cost, payouts and takedowns.

parts.name: Maker portal
parts.what: Where makers upload and sign versions, follow review status, see installs and sales figures, and answer reviews.

parts.name: Maker payouts and tax details
parts.what: Collects makers' payout and tax details through the kit and pays out what their apps earn less the at-cost fee.

parts.name: Rejections and appeals
parts.what: Tells a maker why a version or an app was rejected or removed, with the rule behind it, and how to appeal.

parts.name: Signing key moves
parts.what: Lets a maker rotate an app's signing key or hand the app to a new maker without breaking updates for the people who have it.

features.name: Pay makers in other countries safely
features.does: Know payouts to app makers abroad never reach sanctioned people.

parts.name: Sanctions screening for maker payouts
parts.what: Screens payouts to makers abroad against sanctions lists through the kit before any money is sent.

areas.name: Running Windows and phone programs
areas.summary: Keeping people's existing programs working: a tested list of what runs, Windows programs that start with a double-click through a compatibility layer, a Windows virtual machine for the stubborn few, Android apps, and a plan to replace Windows-only work programs over time.

features.name: Know what will run before switching
features.does: Search a list of Windows programs and see how well each runs on Spare OS before deciding to switch.

parts.name: Compatibility research
parts.what: Which common work programs run through compatibility layers, which don't, and why.

parts.name: Tested compatibility database
parts.what: Open data of programs, versions and how well they run, including whether each works with a screen reader, from our own tests and members' reports.

parts.name: Automated compatibility runs
parts.what: Installs and starts the most common programs on each new release and records whether they still work.

features.name: Double-click a Windows program to run it
features.does: Run a Windows installer or program by double-clicking it, and find it in the start menu afterwards.

parts.name: Compatibility layer packaging
parts.what: Ships the open Windows compatibility layer as a separate program, kept current and tested.

parts.name: Per-program fix recipes
parts.what: Known settings and extra parts each tested program needs, applied automatically when it installs.

parts.name: Sandboxed Windows program launcher
parts.what: Runs each Windows program in its own sandbox by default, with no compatibility-layer drive that maps the whole file system, only the folders it needs and a warning before running one downloaded from the web, and adds start menu entries and a clean uninstall.

parts.name: Windows fonts guidance
parts.what: Never ships Microsoft fonts; uses size-matched open fonts and explains how a person can add fonts they already own.

features.name: Run the stubborn few in Windows
features.does: Run programs that no compatibility layer can handle inside a Windows virtual machine, using a Windows licence the person already owns.

parts.name: Windows virtual machine helper
parts.what: Sets up a Windows virtual machine from the person's own Windows installer and licence, with shared folders.

parts.name: Windows apps in their own windows
parts.what: Shows programs from the virtual machine as ordinary windows on the Spare OS desktop.

parts.name: Licence guidance
parts.what: Explains plainly that Spare OS never supplies Windows and the person needs their own valid licence.

features.name: Report what works
features.does: Report in one click how well a Windows program ran, which feeds the public database.

parts.name: Compatibility report form
parts.what: A short form with the program, version and result, sent with consent and checked before it updates the database.

features.name: Run Android apps
features.does: Run Android apps in a contained space on the PC, installed from open app stores.

parts.name: Android container research
parts.what: Compares open ways to run Android apps on Linux, their hardware needs and the app store terms that apply.

parts.name: Android app support
parts.what: Ships the chosen Android container as an optional, sandboxed add-on, with any Android app store offered under the policy for software that is not open source.

features.name: See Windows-only work programs being replaced
features.does: See which Windows-only programs stop people switching and what the co-op is doing about each one.

parts.name: Switching blockers list
parts.what: Anonymous, opt-in counts of programs and services that blocked people's moves, such as exam device checks and device-compliance rules, from move-across scans and reports.

parts.name: Replacement roadmap
parts.what: Public list linking each top blocker to a Spare program or open project that replaces it, starting with Spare Construct for Revit.

parts.name: NCEA digital exam approval
parts.what: Works with NZQA so Spare OS PCs pass the device check for NCEA digital exams, since its published device guidance names Chrome OS, Windows and Mac and does not mention Linux (current table unverified).

areas.name: Updates, backup and recovery
areas.summary: Updates that install as one piece and roll back if a start-up fails, update metadata that mirrors cannot replay, fast security fixes, whole-PC backups, restore onto a new PC, repair or erase a PC, published support periods, and taking data away in open formats or going back to Windows.

features.name: Get updates that can't break the PC
features.does: Get updates in the background that apply as one piece on the next restart, never half-installed.

parts.name: Image-based update research
parts.what: Compares image-based update systems and how each rolls back.

parts.name: Update server and channels
parts.what: Publishes signed system images and protected update metadata to stable, test and long-support channels, with running costs on the ledger.

parts.name: Background update agent
parts.what: Downloads and stages the next system version while the person works, then switches on restart.

parts.name: Small delta downloads
parts.what: Downloads only what changed between versions, to save data on slow or capped connections.

parts.name: Local network sharing of updates
parts.what: Lets PCs on the same network share updates instead of each downloading them.

parts.name: Update metadata protection
parts.what: Signs update metadata that expires, never lets version numbers go backwards and signs one snapshot of each whole release, as The Update Framework does, so no mirror or peer can freeze updates, serve an old flawed image or mix versions.

parts.name: Mirror and peer rules
parts.what: Terms and a privacy notice for member-run mirrors, saying what they may log and for how long, and a plain warning that peer-to-peer downloads show the person's IP address to other peers.

features.name: Roll back to the last working version
features.does: Choose the previous version at start-up, and have it chosen automatically if a new version fails to start.

parts.name: Start counting and automatic rollback
parts.what: Marks a new version good only after a successful start and falls back if it fails twice.

parts.name: Version choice at start-up
parts.what: Lists the last few versions in the start-up menu with their dates.

features.name: Get security fixes fast
features.does: Get security fixes within days, and urgent ones without waiting for a scheduled update.

parts.name: Security fix line
parts.what: Builds, tests and ships security fixes on a faster track than feature updates.

parts.name: Update timing rules
parts.what: Never restarts mid-work, respects metered and mobile data, and lets people pick restart times.

features.name: Back up the whole PC
features.does: Back up files, apps and settings automatically to a drive, a network folder or Spareware storage, encrypted.

parts.name: Backup engine
parts.what: An open, encrypted, de-duplicating backup tool chosen on licence and proven reliability.

parts.name: Backup app
parts.what: Sets a backup target and schedule in a few clicks and shows when the last good backup ran.

parts.name: Spareware storage backup target
parts.what: Sends encrypted backups to Spareware storage at cost, with only the person holding the key, and any police or court request for them handled through the kit's published process.

features.name: Restore onto a new PC
features.does: Restore files, apps and settings from a backup onto a new or repaired PC.

parts.name: Full restore flow
parts.what: Rebuilds a PC from a backup, reinstalling apps from the store rather than copying them.

features.name: Fix a PC that won't start
features.does: Start a repair mode from the start-up menu or a USB stick, repair the system or reset it while keeping files, or erase it before passing it on.

parts.name: Recovery mode
parts.what: A small repair system that checks the disk, rolls back versions, and copies files off.

parts.name: Reset keeping files
parts.what: Puts the system back to as-new while keeping the person's files and a list of apps to reinstall.

parts.name: Recovery USB maker
parts.what: Makes a recovery USB stick from settings.

parts.name: Erase this PC
parts.what: Erases the PC before it is sold, given away or refurbished, by destroying the disk's encryption key or by a checked wipe, signs it out of the Spareware login and device finding, and reinstalls a fresh system that opens at first-start set-up.

features.name: Know how long my version is supported
features.does: See how long each version gets fixes, and get warned well before it ends with a one-click upgrade.

parts.name: Support period policy
parts.what: A public policy for how long each release gets security fixes, as product security law requires.

parts.name: Version upgrade assistant
parts.what: Checks apps and hardware before a major upgrade and moves the PC across in one step.

features.name: Take my data with me
features.does: Export files, settings and the app list in open, documented formats, delete what the co-op holds, and leave Spare OS cleanly if they choose.

parts.name: Open settings export
parts.what: Exports every setting as a documented, readable file that can be read without Spare OS.

parts.name: Delete my data from co-op services
parts.what: Adds everything Spare OS's services hold, such as synced settings and backups, to the kit's data export and account deletion, and confirms when done.

parts.name: Leaving guide
parts.what: A plain guide to moving files and settings to another system, including back to Windows.

parts.name: Give the PC back to Windows
parts.what: Removes Spare OS from a PC that also has Windows, returns the disk space and the start-up menu to Windows, and checks Windows starts before finishing.

parts.name: Export passwords and contacts
parts.what: Exports the password vault, contacts and calendars in open formats other systems can import.

areas.name: Security and privacy
areas.summary: Safe by default: full-disk encryption, a signed start-up chain with Secure Boot, a firewall, sandboxed apps, a privacy dashboard with nothing shared by default, passwords and passkeys, a security team that publishes fixes, and help with lost laptops.

features.name: Encrypt the whole disk
features.does: Have the disk encrypted by default, unlocked with a password or the PC's security chip, with a recovery key kept safe.

parts.name: Full-disk encryption
parts.what: Encrypts the system and home folders with proven open disk encryption.

parts.name: Security chip unlock
parts.what: Unlocks the disk automatically on the same unchanged PC using its TPM, with a PIN option.

parts.name: Recovery key safe-keeping
parts.what: Lets the person print the recovery key or save it to their Spareware account; organisations keep keys in their directory through OS-A19-F1-P4.

parts.name: Accessible start-up unlock screen
parts.what: The disk unlock screen speaks or beeps, works with a braille display where possible, uses the keyboard layout the passphrase was set with, shows clearly that it is waiting and uses large text, since everyone meets it before the screen reader loads.

features.name: Start up securely
features.does: Keep Secure Boot on, so only signed start-up files and drivers load.

parts.name: Signed start-up chain
parts.what: Gets the first-stage boot loader signed by the certificate authority PC firmware trusts, and keeps up with certificate changes such as the 2026 expiry of the 2011 certificates.

parts.name: Signed drivers and modules
parts.what: Signs kernel modules and extra drivers with Spare OS keys, and enrols the key for drivers built on the PC.

parts.name: Revocation list updates
parts.what: Applies firmware revocation list updates so known-bad boot loaders are blocked.

parts.name: Signing accounts and agreements
parts.what: The accounts and agreements the co-op needs to have boot files signed, held by the legal entity.

features.name: Block attacks from the network
features.does: Have a firewall on by default, with simple choices for home, work and public networks.

parts.name: Firewall and network profiles
parts.what: Blocks incoming connections by default and asks in plain words when an app wants to accept them.

features.name: Keep each app in its own box
features.does: Know that apps can't read other apps' data or reach the camera, microphone, files or location without asking.

parts.name: App sandbox and permission prompts
parts.what: Runs store apps in sandboxes and asks the person when an app needs something outside its box.

parts.name: In-use indicators
parts.what: Shows a clear sign whenever the camera, microphone, screen sharing or location is in use, and by which app.

features.name: See and control my data
features.does: See what Spare OS and each app send, with usage statistics off unless the person turns them on.

parts.name: Privacy dashboard
parts.what: One page showing each kind of data, who can reach it and what is sent, with switches.

parts.name: Opt-in usage statistics
parts.what: Collects only counts people agree to, aggregates them so no one is identifiable, and publishes the results, moving onto the kit's private usage counts (KIT-A22-F8-P1) once the kit brings them forward.

features.name: Scan files from other systems
features.does: Scan downloads and USB drives for malware, mainly to avoid passing Windows malware on to others.

parts.name: On-demand malware scanner
parts.what: An open malware scanner run on request or on new drives, with signature updates.

features.name: Keep passwords and passkeys safe
features.does: Store passwords and passkeys in a built-in vault and sign in to sites with passkeys.

parts.name: System keyring
parts.what: Stores app passwords and keys encrypted and unlocked with the person's sign-in.

parts.name: Password manager and passkeys
parts.what: A password and passkey manager that works in the browser and apps and can import from others, with syncing between PCs added by OS-A12-F11.

features.name: Hear about security problems and report them
features.does: Report a security flaw safely, and read plain advisories on what was fixed and what to do.

parts.name: Security response team and disclosure policy
parts.what: A named team and set response times for Spare OS, taking reports through the kit's page for reporting weaknesses.

parts.name: Security advisories
parts.what: Public advisories for each fix, in plain words and in a machine-readable form.

features.name: Find, lock or wipe a lost laptop
features.does: Find a lost laptop's last known place, lock it or wipe it from another device.

parts.name: Find my device
parts.what: Reports location only when the owner turns it on and asks, through the accounts and maps services.

parts.name: Remote lock and wipe
parts.what: Locks or erases a lost PC from the owner's account or the organisation's console.

parts.name: Requests for device locations and backups
parts.what: Sends police and court requests for device locations and backups held by co-op services through the kit's published process, counts them in the transparency report, and keeps the data where the data-location rules say.

parts.name: Stalking safeguards
parts.what: Tells every user of a shared or family PC when device finding is on and when it was last used, never lets another account turn it on silently, and shows the person at the PC a clear notice they can act on.

features.name: Sign in with fingerprint or face
features.does: Sign in and approve admin prompts with a fingerprint or a face camera.

parts.name: Fingerprint sign-in
parts.what: Uses the fingerprint readers supported in OS-A14-F9-P1 for sign-in and admin prompts, with the print stored only on the device.

parts.name: Face sign-in research
parts.what: Checks open face sign-in for infrared cameras against photo and spoofing attacks before offering it.

features.name: Sync passwords between my PCs
features.does: Keep passwords, passkeys and Wi-Fi passwords the same on all their PCs, encrypted so only they can read them.

parts.name: End-to-end encrypted secrets sync
parts.what: Syncs the password vault, passkeys and Wi-Fi passwords between the person's PCs end-to-end encrypted, on the kit's chosen encryption.

areas.name: Users, sign-in and family
areas.summary: Who uses the PC and how they get in: separate users, guests, Spareware login with offline sign-in, child accounts and parental controls, password recovery and safe admin prompts.

features.name: Have separate users on one PC
features.does: Give each person their own account, files and settings on a shared PC.

parts.name: User accounts service
parts.what: Creates, changes and removes users through system commands, standard users by default.

parts.name: Private home folders
parts.what: Keeps each user's files encrypted and readable only by them.

features.name: Let a guest use the PC
features.does: Let a visitor use the PC in a guest session that is wiped when they sign out.

parts.name: Guest session
parts.what: A temporary account with no access to other users' files, erased at sign-out.

features.name: Sign in with a Spareware login
features.does: Sign in to the PC with a Spareware login and keep signing in when offline.

parts.name: Spareware login on the sign-in screen
parts.what: Signs in through the accounts service using standard open sign-in protocols, with passkeys first.

parts.name: Offline sign-in
parts.what: Keeps a secure local copy of the sign-in so the person can get in without internet.

features.name: Keep children safe
features.does: Set up child accounts with screen time, age-suitable apps, spending limits and web filtering, managed from a parent's account.

parts.name: Child accounts and family settings
parts.what: Links child accounts to parents and applies age-based defaults from the age range and app age ratings, following the kit's rules for parents and carers.

parts.name: Screen time limits
parts.what: Daily limits and bedtimes per child, with a request for more time.

parts.name: Web filter for children
parts.what: Optional family-safe filtering of websites at the network level, with the filter's rules visible to parents.

parts.name: Parent's view
parts.what: Lets parents see and approve requests from their own phone or PC.

features.name: Get back in after forgetting a password
features.does: Reset a forgotten password with a recovery key, another admin, or the Spareware login.

parts.name: Password recovery flow
parts.what: Offers each recovery route the person set up, without ever weakening disk encryption.

features.name: Make admin changes safely
features.does: Approve system changes with an admin password when needed, and use the PC as a standard user day to day.

parts.name: Admin prompts
parts.what: Clear prompts saying exactly what will change, logged as system commands.

areas.name: Devices and connections
areas.summary: Getting online and using hardware: Wi-Fi and mobile data, work and school networks, VPNs, printers and scanners, Bluetooth, the person's phone, pens, cameras and sound, fingerprint readers and smart cards, screens, projectors and docks, private location, and true colours on screen and in print.

features.name: Get online
features.does: Connect to Wi-Fi, wired networks, phone hotspots and mobile data, including networks with a sign-in page.

parts.name: Network connections
parts.what: Manages Wi-Fi, wired, hotspot and mobile data connections with an open network manager.

parts.name: Sign-in page detection
parts.what: Spots cafe and hotel networks that need a sign-in page and opens it safely.

parts.name: Mobile data and phone hotspots
parts.what: Supports built-in mobile data modems and hotspots, counting data on capped connections.

parts.name: Work and school Wi-Fi and proxies
parts.what: Connects to enterprise Wi-Fi that uses certificates, including eduroam, and follows system proxy and automatic proxy settings.

parts.name: One trusted certificate store
parts.what: One place to install a trusted root certificate that the browser, sandboxed apps and the compatibility layer all honour, as school networks that inspect encrypted traffic, such as N4L's, need.

features.name: Use a VPN
features.does: Connect to a work or personal VPN, including the common types offices use.

parts.name: VPN connections
parts.what: Supports the common open VPN types, plus the open clients that connect to popular office VPN products.

features.name: Print
features.does: Print to home and office printers, most with no driver at all, and share a printer.

parts.name: Printing system
parts.what: An open printing system with driverless printing for modern printers and automatic discovery on the network.

parts.name: Driver packs for older printers
parts.what: Open drivers for older printers, matched by model, with the compatibility list showing what works.

parts.name: Print dialog
parts.what: One print dialog for every app, with preview, page choices and paper sizes.

features.name: Scan documents
features.does: Scan from scanners and all-in-one printers, and turn scans into searchable PDFs.

parts.name: Scanning system
parts.what: Open scanning support with driverless scanning for modern devices.

parts.name: Scan app
parts.what: Scans single pages or many into a PDF, with text recognition so the PDF can be searched.

features.name: Pair Bluetooth devices
features.does: Pair headphones, speakers, mice, keyboards and controllers, and switch between them easily.

parts.name: Bluetooth support
parts.what: Open Bluetooth support with good audio quality codecs and simple pairing.

features.name: Link my phone
features.does: Send files and links between phone and PC, see phone notifications on the PC, and use the phone as a remote.

parts.name: Phone link
parts.what: Pairs Android and iPhone over the local network using an open phone-link protocol, with the phone side built per the phone apps decision.

parts.name: Nearby sharing between PCs
parts.what: Sends files to nearby Spare OS PCs on the same network with the receiver's consent.

parts.name: Phone as a webcam
parts.what: Uses the person's phone as a webcam for calls over the phone link.

features.name: Use pens and drawing tablets
features.does: Use a pen on a touch screen or a drawing tablet with pressure, tilt and buttons set per app.

parts.name: Pen and tablet support
parts.what: Open drivers and a settings page for pens and drawing tablets, including button mapping.

features.name: Use cameras, microphones and speakers
features.does: Use built-in and USB cameras, microphones and speakers, and switch between them from the tray.

parts.name: Cameras and screen sharing
parts.what: Makes cameras and screen sharing work through the modern media system with per-app permission.

parts.name: Sound devices and mixer
parts.what: Handles speakers, headsets and microphones, per-app volume and automatic switching when a headset is plugged in.

parts.name: Built-in laptop cameras
parts.what: Checks the MIPI cameras common on Intel laptops from 2022 on, which have weak Linux support, and gets the ones that can work going so video calls don't break.

features.name: Use fingerprint readers, smart cards and security keys
features.does: Use a fingerprint reader, a work smart card or a hardware security key.

parts.name: Fingerprint readers
parts.what: Supports the fingerprint readers that have open drivers, listed on the compatibility list.

parts.name: Smart cards and security keys
parts.what: Supports smart cards for government and office sign-in and hardware security keys for websites.

features.name: Use screens, projectors and docks
features.does: Plug in monitors, projectors and USB-C or Thunderbolt docks, and show the screen on a TV.

parts.name: Screen hotplug and projector mode
parts.what: Detects new screens and offers duplicate, extend or second-screen-only in one step.

parts.name: Cast to a TV
parts.what: Shows the screen on smart TVs and streaming boxes through open casting protocols where they exist.

parts.name: Docks and Thunderbolt approval
parts.what: Supports docks and asks before trusting a new Thunderbolt device.

features.name: Share my location only when I choose
features.does: Let the PC and chosen apps know roughly where it is for time zones, maps, weather and finding a lost laptop, only with consent.

parts.name: Private location lookup
parts.what: Works out location from nearby Wi-Fi through an open provider that speaks the retired Mozilla service's protocol, such as beaconDB, or one the co-op runs at cost on the maps service, since Linux lost its usual source when Mozilla's closed in 2024; patent claims like those that led Mozilla to settle are checked before the co-op runs its own.

parts.name: Location data rules
parts.what: Says what is sent to look up a location, what is kept and for how long, and asks consent before the first lookup.

features.name: See true colours on screen and in print
features.does: Have colours match across screens and printers, and calibrate screens, including HDR ones.

parts.name: Colour profiles
parts.what: Applies a colour profile to each monitor and printer so every app shows and prints the same colours.

parts.name: Screen calibration
parts.what: Calibrates screens with a measuring device and sets up high dynamic range screens, for people who design for print.

features.name: Look and sound better on calls
features.does: Remove background noise from the microphone, and blur or frame the camera background, in any call app.

parts.name: Voice and camera effects
parts.what: Noise suppression for microphones, and background blur and framing for cameras, run on the device and offered to every app as virtual devices.

areas.name: Accessibility
areas.summary: Usable by everyone from the first screen, including the disk unlock screen: a screen reader with braille and familiar commands, magnifier, high contrast and colour filters, other ways to type and click, voice control and dictation, live captions, hearing support, natural voices including te reo Māori, and the accessibility law Spare OS must meet.

features.name: Use a screen reader
features.does: Use the whole system and every Spare app with a screen reader, from the first start, including on a braille display.

parts.name: Screen reader
parts.what: Ships an open screen reader set up to start by shortcut, with every built-in app labelled for it.

parts.name: Braille displays
parts.what: Supports common refreshable braille displays through the screen reader.

parts.name: Accessibility checks for every screen
parts.what: Automated and human checks that every Spare OS screen, including the start-up menu and the disk unlock screen, works with the screen reader and keyboard alone.

parts.name: Unlock without seeing the screen
parts.what: A tested way into an encrypted PC for people who cannot use the unlock screen, such as unlocking with the security chip on an unchanged PC or with a trusted helper, checked with blind testers each release.

parts.name: Familiar screen reader commands
parts.what: Our own screen reader key map that people coming from NVDA or JAWS will find familiar, plus guides for blind people switching from Windows.

features.name: Zoom in and make things bigger
features.does: Zoom the screen, make text and the pointer larger, and keep it that way everywhere.

parts.name: Magnifier
parts.what: Full-screen and lens zoom that follows the pointer, keyboard focus and typing.

parts.name: Text and pointer size
parts.what: System-wide text scaling and pointer size that all built-in apps honour.

features.name: See the screen clearly
features.does: Use high contrast, colour filters for colour blindness, and less motion and transparency.

parts.name: High contrast and colour filters
parts.what: High-contrast themes, colour-blind filters and reduce-motion settings applied across the desktop and apps.

features.name: Type and click another way
features.does: Use sticky keys, slow keys, mouse keys, an on-screen keyboard, switch access or dwell clicking.

parts.name: Keyboard access options
parts.what: Sticky, slow and bounce keys and mouse keys, each turned on from settings or a shortcut.

parts.name: Switch access and dwell click
parts.what: Scanning switch access and dwell clicking for people who use one or two switches or head pointers.

features.name: Control the PC by voice
features.does: Open apps, click, scroll and type by voice, offline.

parts.name: Voice control
parts.what: Spoken commands mapped to system commands, with numbered labels on screen to click by voice, on the shared speech engine, handing commands for Spare apps to the kit's voice control (KIT-A17-F8-P1) once the kit builds it, so there is one voice path, not two.

parts.name: Dictation into any text box
parts.what: Types what the person says into any app, with spoken punctuation and corrections.

features.name: Read captions for any sound
features.does: See live captions for any sound playing on the PC, made on the device.

parts.name: Live captions
parts.what: Captions for any audio, including calls and videos, in a movable window, made on the device.

features.name: Hear text read aloud
features.does: Have any text read aloud in a natural voice, including NZ English and te reo Māori.

parts.name: Text-to-speech voices
parts.what: Open, natural voices for the main languages, used by the screen reader and read-aloud.

parts.name: Te reo Māori voice
parts.what: Works with Māori language and data experts on a te reo Māori voice on terms that respect Māori data sovereignty.

features.name: Rely on Spare OS meeting accessibility law
features.does: Rely on Spare OS meeting accessibility law and standards wherever it is offered, such as the European Accessibility Act, which covers consumer operating systems.

parts.name: Accessibility conformance report
parts.what: A published report against the European standard for accessible technology and WCAG, updated each release.

parts.name: Accessibility law research
parts.what: Which accessibility laws apply to a free operating system in NZ, the EU and other markets, and what each requires; the research belongs in the kit for every Spare app.

features.name: Use eye or head tracking
features.does: Move the pointer and click with eye or head tracking hardware.

parts.name: Eye and head tracking research
parts.what: Finds which trackers have open drivers and how they fit with dwell clicking.

features.name: Use the PC with hearing loss
features.does: Hear sound in one ear or with uneven hearing, and see a flash when the PC plays an alert sound.

parts.name: Mono audio, balance and visual alerts
parts.what: Mono audio, left and right balance, and a screen flash for alert sounds, each set from accessibility settings.

features.name: Pair my hearing aids
features.does: Pair Bluetooth LE Audio hearing aids and hear the PC through them.

parts.name: Hearing aid pairing
parts.what: Pairs Bluetooth LE Audio hearing aids and streams sound to them, tested on the lab's hearing aids.

areas.name: Languages and regions
areas.summary: New Zealand first, international by design: every screen translatable, te reo Māori and Pacific languages first-class with their own keyboards, dictionaries and te reo speech, every keyboard and script, local formats, spelling, country packs and on-device translation.

features.name: Use Spare OS in my language
features.does: Use every screen of Spare OS in their own language, with te reo Māori and NZ English ready from the start.

parts.name: Translation workflow
parts.what: Spare OS's texts on the kit's member translation workflow, with review before release, linked to the translation platforms of the open projects Spare OS ships.

parts.name: Te reo Māori translation
parts.what: A full te reo Māori translation done with Māori language experts, with agreed terms for new technical words.

parts.name: Pacific languages
parts.what: Translations for Samoan, Tongan, Cook Islands Māori and other Pacific languages, led by native speakers.

parts.name: Text built for translation
parts.what: Every interface text kept in translatable form through the kit's translation framework, with room for longer words and plural rules.

features.name: Type in any language
