features.does: Type in any language with the right keyboard layout or input method, including macrons for te reo Māori.

parts.name: Keyboard layouts and input methods
parts.what: Ships open input methods for Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indic and other scripts, switched from the tray.

parts.name: Māori macrons by default
parts.what: Sets NZ keyboards to type macron vowels with a simple key combination out of the box.

parts.name: Pacific keyboards
parts.what: Ready-to-use Samoan, Tongan and Cook Islands Māori keyboard layouts that type the ʻokina or fakauʻa and macrons.

features.name: See every script and emoji
features.does: Read every writing system and emoji correctly, including right-to-left languages.

parts.name: Fonts for all scripts and emoji
parts.what: Open font families that cover every major writing system and current emoji.

parts.name: Right-to-left checks
parts.what: Checks that every Spare OS screen lays out correctly in right-to-left languages.

features.name: Use local formats
features.does: See dates, times, numbers, money, paper size and units the local way.

parts.name: Regional formats
parts.what: Regional settings for dates, numbers, currency, A4 or Letter paper and metric or imperial units.

features.name: Check spelling in my language
features.does: Get spell checking in their language in every app, including te reo Māori and NZ English.

parts.name: Spelling dictionaries
parts.what: Open spelling dictionaries for each supported language, shared by all apps.

parts.name: Pacific spelling dictionaries
parts.what: Spelling dictionaries for Samoan, Tongan, Cook Islands Māori and other Pacific languages, built with native speakers on terms they agree.

features.name: Get a set-up that fits my country
features.does: Get the right public holidays, emergency information, legal notices and download mirrors for their country.

parts.name: Country packs
parts.what: Spare OS's own settings, such as default mirrors and local help contacts, added to the kit's country packs, starting with New Zealand.

parts.name: Local mirrors per country
parts.what: Download and update mirrors in each country where members run them.

features.name: Translate text on the device
features.does: Translate text and web pages without sending them anywhere.

parts.name: Offline translation
parts.what: Runs open translation models on the device for chosen language pairs.

features.name: Speak to the PC in te reo Māori
features.does: Dictate, see captions and control the PC by voice in te reo Māori, not only in English.

parts.name: Te reo Māori speech recognition
parts.what: Builds te reo Māori speech recognition for dictation, live captions and voice control with Māori language and data experts, respecting the community licence terms that existing te reo speech data comes with.

areas.name: Games and media
areas.summary: Play and watch: Windows games through game store apps and a compatibility layer, controllers, every common media format shipped legally, paid streaming services, game performance, recording, and low-delay audio for musicians.

features.name: Play Windows games
features.does: Install game store apps and play most Windows games, and see which games will not run and why.

parts.name: Game store apps
parts.what: Packages the main game store apps that support Linux, with their compatibility tools set up, offered under the policy for software that is not open source.

parts.name: Anti-cheat compatibility list
parts.what: Lists popular games whose anti-cheat blocks them on Linux, so people know before switching.

features.name: Use game controllers
features.does: Plug in or pair common game controllers and have them work in games straight away.

parts.name: Controller support
parts.what: Open drivers and settings for common controllers, including wireless ones.

features.name: Play every common media format
features.does: Play common audio and video formats, with patent licences handled properly.

parts.name: Codec licensing research
parts.what: Which common video and audio formats carry patent licences, and how other distributions ship them legally.

parts.name: Hardware video decoding
parts.what: Uses the graphics chip to play video smoothly and save battery.

features.name: Watch paid streaming services
features.does: Watch subscription video services in the browser at their full supported quality.

parts.name: Browser content protection
parts.what: Offers the content protection module streaming sites need, on terms its owner allows and under the policy for software that is not open source.

features.name: Get the best game performance
features.does: Turn on a game mode, see frame rates, and use high dynamic range and variable refresh screens.

parts.name: Game mode and performance overlay
parts.what: Raises a game's priority, pauses background work and shows frame rate when asked.

parts.name: High dynamic range and variable refresh
parts.what: Supports high dynamic range and variable refresh screens in games and video.

features.name: Record and stream gameplay
features.does: Record game clips and stream to any service the person chooses.

parts.name: Game capture
parts.what: Records the last few minutes on a shortcut and streams with low overhead.

features.name: Make music with low delay
features.does: Use audio interfaces and music software with low delay for recording and live playing.

parts.name: Low-delay audio set-up
parts.what: A one-switch set-up for low-delay audio, tested with common audio interfaces.

areas.name: AI, commands and automation
areas.summary: Headless by rule: every system action is a command and every state can be read by a query, used the same way by people, scripts, plugins and AI, with an MCP server any AI can drive under the person's approval, a registry of app MCP servers, agents kept in their own workspace, an optional on-device assistant, a shared on-device engine for text and speech recognition, routines and desktop plugins.

features.name: Run any system action as a command
features.does: Do anything the settings and system tools do through a typed command or a script, with a log and undo.

parts.name: System command layer
parts.what: Every setting and system action is an operation on the kit's command layer, shared by the interface, scripts, plugins and AI.

parts.name: Command catalogue
parts.what: A documented, searchable list of every system command, its inputs and the permission it needs.

parts.name: Change log and undo
parts.what: Records every system change with who or what made it, and undoes settings changes.

parts.name: System queries
parts.what: Read-only queries for state such as installed apps, battery, logs and settings, so people, scripts and agents can look without changing anything.

features.name: Let an AI help with the PC
features.does: Let any AI assistant the person chooses check and change the PC through MCP, approving each sensitive step.

parts.name: System MCP server
parts.what: An MCP server over the system command layer, off until the person turns it on.

parts.name: Approvals and limits for AI actions
parts.what: Applies the kit's approval steps and agent limits to system actions, asking the person before anything sensitive and logging every step.

parts.name: Hidden instruction guards on the PC
parts.what: Uses the kit's hidden instruction guards on everything an agent reads on the PC, such as files, windows and web pages.

parts.name: Registry of app MCP servers
parts.what: One system list of every installed app's MCP server, with one consent screen for which agents may use which, as Windows now has with its on-device registry.

parts.name: Agent workspace
parts.what: Runs agents that drive the desktop in an isolated workspace or as a separate low-privilege user, so they never act with the person's full rights.

parts.name: Approvals only a person can give
parts.what: Shows admin, payment and agent approvals on a secure screen that agents, scripts and synthetic input cannot press, while the person's own keyboard, switch access and voice control still can.

features.name: Ask for help in plain words
features.does: Ask how to do something or to fix a problem, and get an answer or the fix, using an on-device model by default.

parts.name: Assistant panel
parts.what: A panel from the taskbar to ask questions and approve suggested fixes, built on the kit's help assistant.

parts.name: On-device assistant model
parts.what: Runs an open language model for the assistant on the shared on-device AI engine, with nothing leaving the PC.

parts.name: Model choice and licences
parts.what: Chooses on-device models whose licences allow shipping them, under the kit's AI tools policy, and lets people plug in a cloud AI of their choice.

parts.name: AI transparency duties
parts.what: Tells people they are talking to an AI and marks AI-made content, as Article 50 of the EU AI Act has required since 2 August 2026, and lists the assistant on the co-op's AI use register.

features.name: Recognise text and speech on the device
features.does: Have apps read text in images, turn speech into text and speak in natural voices, without sending anything away.

parts.name: Text and speech recognition services
parts.what: Text recognition and speech recognition on the shared engine, used by screenshots, scanning, captions, dictation and voice control.

parts.name: Shared on-device AI engine
parts.what: Runs open models on the processor, graphics chip or AI chip for text recognition, speech recognition and text-to-speech, with nothing leaving the PC; it belongs in a shared engine so every Spare desktop app on Windows and macOS can use it too.

features.name: Automate routines
features.does: Set routines such as opening work apps when joining the work Wi-Fi, or running a clean-up every week.

parts.name: Routines engine
parts.what: Runs chains of system commands on triggers like time, network, device or battery.

parts.name: Routines editor
parts.what: Builds routines from plain choices, with no code needed.

features.name: Add plugins to the desktop
features.does: Add sandboxed plugins that extend the desktop, tray or file manager.

parts.name: Desktop plugin host
parts.what: Runs desktop plugins as sandboxed components with declared permissions.

areas.name: Managing many machines
areas.summary: For offices, schools and co-ops: central sign-in, setting up many PCs at once with their network settings, rules and admin roles for every machine, update control, inventory, IT remote help, classrooms, exams and shared PCs, local admin passwords, joining existing Microsoft and Google networks, an office server, fleet security and local IT partners, all without paid licences.

features.name: Sign in with a work or school account on any PC
features.does: Sign in to any of the organisation's PCs with one work or school account.

parts.name: Directory and sign-in research
parts.what: Compares open directory, sign-in and device management tools for offices and schools.

parts.name: Directory service
parts.what: Ships the chosen open directory and sign-in service as an easy-to-run package for an organisation's own server, bringing people in through the kit's organisation directory sync, which Spare Office uses too.

parts.name: Join a PC to a directory
parts.what: Joins a PC to the organisation's directory from first start or settings in a few steps.

parts.name: Recovery keys in the directory
parts.what: Stores each joined PC's disk recovery key in the organisation's directory, readable only by named IT staff, with every look logged.

features.name: Set up many PCs at once
features.does: Enrol new PCs and have them set themselves up with the right apps, settings and Wi-Fi.

parts.name: Enrolment and set-up service
parts.what: Enrols PCs from first start or a network install and applies the organisation's set-up profile.

parts.name: Set-up profiles
parts.what: Documented files that list apps, settings, Wi-Fi and rules for each group of PCs.

parts.name: Network and certificate profiles
parts.what: Pushes work Wi-Fi, proxy settings and trusted certificates to every enrolled PC from the console.

features.name: Set rules for every PC
features.does: Set rules such as password strength, blocked USB drives, allowed apps and screen lock times for groups of PCs.

parts.name: Rules engine
parts.what: Applies and reports rules on each PC through the system command layer, even offline.

parts.name: Management console
parts.what: A web console to set rules, see PCs and act on them, with every admin action logged, plugged into the kit's organisation team management so device rules and Spare Office admin can share one console, which belongs in the kit.

parts.name: Admin roles and IT scripts
parts.what: Role-based admin, such as teacher, IT staff and auditor, each limited to its own actions, with the same actions open to IT scripts through the command API and MCP.

parts.name: Firmware settings from the console
parts.what: Sets start-up firmware options, such as boot order and firmware passwords, across PCs through the interfaces PC makers publish.

features.name: Control updates across PCs
features.does: Roll updates out to test groups first, pause them, and serve them from a local cache.

parts.name: Update rings and local cache
parts.what: Groups PCs into rings with set delays and caches updates on a local server.

features.name: See every PC's state
features.does: See every PC's model, version, encryption, last update and health in one list and export it.

parts.name: Inventory and compliance reports
parts.what: Collects each PC's state and shows which ones break the organisation's rules.

features.name: Help colleagues and reach PCs as IT staff
features.does: As IT staff, help a colleague on their screen under the organisation's rules, and connect to the organisation's PCs by remote desktop.

parts.name: Remote help for IT staff
parts.what: Lets the organisation's IT staff start the same consented, logged help sessions with colleagues, under the organisation's rules and admin roles.

parts.name: Remote desktop
parts.what: Open remote desktop server and client that also connect to Windows PCs.

features.name: Run classrooms and shared PCs
features.does: Run lab and library PCs that reset after each person, single-app kiosks, and exam mode.

parts.name: Kiosk and shared PC modes
parts.what: Locks a PC to one app or resets it to a clean state at each sign-out.

parts.name: Classroom tools
parts.what: Lets a teacher share their screen, send files and pause screens, with students told when it is on.

parts.name: Exam mode
parts.what: Locks the PC to an exam app or site for the length of an exam.

parts.name: Exam platforms that check the system
parts.what: Tracks exam and assessment platforms that check which operating system a device runs, as NZQA's does, and works with each so exam mode meets them.

features.name: Keep local admin passwords safe
features.does: Have a different local admin password on each PC, changed automatically and stored in the directory.

parts.name: Local admin password rotation
parts.what: Sets and rotates each PC's local admin password and saves it in the directory.

features.name: Fit into an existing Microsoft network
features.does: Join existing Windows domains and cloud directories, use their file shares and printers, and pass their device rules.

parts.name: Windows domain and cloud directory join
parts.what: Joins existing Windows domains and Microsoft cloud directories with open tools built from published protocols.

parts.name: Microsoft 365 device compliance
parts.what: Checks whether Microsoft 365 rules that only admit compliant devices will accept Spare OS PCs, and what an organisation can do if they don't.

features.name: Get help from a local IT partner
features.does: Hire a local IT firm trained and listed by the co-op to run Spare OS PCs.

parts.name: IT partner programme
parts.what: How local IT firms are trained, listed and rated to support Spare OS for organisations.

features.name: Fit into Google Workspace
features.does: Sign in with a Google Workspace for Education or business account and manage PCs from it, as many NZ schools do with Chromebooks.

parts.name: Google Workspace sign-in and management
parts.what: Signs in to Spare OS PCs with Google Workspace accounts through Google's published sign-in standards, and takes settings from Google's admin tools where its terms allow.

features.name: Run the office server
features.does: Run file shares, printing, network addresses, backups and update caching for an office or school on one server, without a Windows Server licence.

parts.name: File and print serving
parts.what: File shares with permissions and quotas, and a print server with shared queues, from open servers that speak Windows' published protocols, installed beside the directory service.

parts.name: Network services and backup target
parts.what: DNS and DHCP, a network backup target and the update cache in the same package, set up from one screen.

features.name: Keep a fleet secure
features.does: Collect logs centrally, get alerts about suspicious activity, check each PC's health, and show the fleet meets a recognised security baseline.

parts.name: Central logs and alerts
parts.what: Collects logs from every PC on the organisation's server and alerts IT staff to suspicious activity, using open detection rules.

parts.name: Device health checks
parts.what: Lets the console check, through each PC's security chip, that it started securely and has not been tampered with.

parts.name: Hardening baselines
parts.what: Published security baselines for Spare OS, checked against the NZ Information Security Manual and common benchmarks, that the rules engine can apply and report on.

features.name: Pick approved apps myself
features.does: As staff, choose and install apps the organisation has approved, without asking IT each time.

parts.name: Organisation app catalogue
parts.what: A private catalogue of the apps an organisation approves, shown in the store to its staff.

areas.name: Help, support and community
areas.summary: People need help switching: built-in guides that also work offline, a member support network, safe remote help from verified helpers, a community forum, one-click problem reports, complaints that get put right, a say on Spare OS, what it costs to run and how that is paid, release notes and status, and early test versions.

features.name: Get help inside Spare OS
features.does: Search plain guides inside Spare OS, including how to do familiar Windows tasks, and run fixers for common problems.

parts.name: Help app and guides
parts.what: Shows the kit's help centre guides for Spare OS in every supported language, written in short sentences with pictures.

parts.name: Fixers for common problems
parts.what: Step-by-step checks that find and fix common Wi-Fi, sound, printer, screen and update problems.

parts.name: Guides that work offline
parts.what: Keeps the main guides on the PC, in recovery mode and on the USB stick, so they work when Wi-Fi, start-up or the screen has failed.

parts.name: Help on a phone
parts.what: A phone-friendly help site with fixes for a PC that won't start or connect.

features.name: Get help from a person
features.does: Get help from a trained member by chat, call or in person, free for basics and at cost for businesses.

parts.name: Member support network
parts.what: Matches people who need help with trained member helpers, by language and place.

parts.name: Helper training and badges
parts.what: The helper course and badge on the kit's training and certificates, with ratings from the people helpers help.

parts.name: Business support at cost
parts.what: Paid support plans for organisations priced at cost and shown on the ledger.

parts.name: Phone and NZ Relay support
parts.what: Help by phone, and through NZ Relay for Deaf, hard of hearing and speech-impaired people, for when the PC itself is what's broken.

features.name: Ask the community
features.does: Ask and answer questions in a community forum linked from Spare OS.

parts.name: Community forum
parts.what: Spare OS's part of the kit's member forum, signed in with the Spareware login.

features.name: Report a problem
features.does: Report a problem in one click, seeing exactly what diagnostic details will be sent before sending.

parts.name: Diagnostics collector
parts.what: Gathers logs and system details for a problem, removes personal details and shows the result to the person.

parts.name: Problem report form
parts.what: A short form that sends the report to the public tracker or a helper, with the person's consent.

parts.name: Crash reports with consent
parts.what: Collects crash reports only when the person agrees, and groups them so fixes go where they matter, moving onto the kit's crash reports (KIT-A22-F9-P1) once the kit brings them forward.

features.name: Have a say on Spare OS
features.does: Propose and vote on Spare OS defaults and priorities as a member.

parts.name: Votes on defaults and priorities
parts.what: Links Spare OS proposals to the member voting service, where only people, never agents, can vote.

parts.name: Who votes on Spare OS
parts.what: Sets who votes on Spare OS (users who are members, helpers, contributors or all members), what can be voted on, such as defaults, store rules, priorities and the funding model, and what no vote can override, such as legal duties and security fixes.

features.name: See what Spare OS costs to run
features.does: See each month what the build servers, mirrors, test lab, signing and support cost.

parts.name: Spare OS ledger entries
parts.what: Publishes the running costs of Spare OS on the open cost ledger each month.

features.name: Test new versions early
features.does: Join a test channel to try new versions early and send feedback.

parts.name: Test channel and feedback
parts.what: A test update channel with an in-app feedback button and the option to return to stable.

features.name: Get help remotely, safely
features.does: Let a verified helper see or control the screen for a set task and time, after agreeing, with a record kept and an easy way to report a scam.

parts.name: Remote help sessions
parts.what: Screen sharing and control the person approves each time, limited to a scope and a time, with a visible banner, one-click stop and a log kept for the person.

parts.name: Verified helpers only
parts.what: Lets only helpers whose identity the kit has checked start a session, and shows their verified name and badge throughout.

parts.name: Scam warning and report
parts.what: Warns before every session that the co-op never calls out of the blue and gives a one-click report, since built-in remote help is the main tool of tech-support scams, as in the 2024 ransomware attacks through Windows' Quick Assist.

features.name: Know a helper who visits is safety-checked
features.does: Know that helpers who come to their home or work with vulnerable people have passed a safety check.

parts.name: Safety checks for visiting helpers
parts.what: Requires a consented safety check through the kit before a helper visits homes or helps vulnerable people, and in-person help starts only once this is in place.

features.name: Know how Spare OS's running costs are paid
features.does: See who pays for the build servers, mirrors, test lab, signing, security team and support, since a free system has no jobs to charge a fee on.

parts.name: Funding model
parts.what: Compares ways to pay Spare OS's running costs, such as member dues, donations, business support plans, partner PC fees and a share of co-op costs, as a decision note for members.

parts.name: Funding vote and ledger lines
parts.what: Puts the chosen funding model to a member vote and shows each funding source on the ledger beside the costs it pays.

features.name: Put things right when help goes wrong
features.does: Complain or open a dispute about a helper, paid business support, an IT partner or a store purchase, and know paid helpers work under the co-op's worker and safety rules.

parts.name: Complaints and disputes about help
parts.what: Takes complaints and disputes about helpers, paid support, IT partners and store purchases through the kit's disputes, with a path to put right a broken PC or lost data.

parts.name: Rules for paid helpers and IT partners
parts.what: Applies the kit's worker-status, health and safety and insurance rules to paid helpers and IT partners who take control of PCs or go into homes.

features.name: Know what changed and what's down
features.does: Read plain release notes and known issues, and check one page when updates, mirrors or the store fail.

parts.name: Release notes and known issues
parts.what: Plain-words release notes for every update and a list of known issues with workarounds.

parts.name: Status of updates, mirrors and store
parts.what: Shows the health of the update server, mirrors and store on the kit's status page.

areas.name: Legal duties and licences
areas.summary: What Spare OS must do by law and by licence wherever it is offered: licence notices and source for every shipped part, a policy for software that is not open source, product security law, age-assurance laws, app takedowns and platform law, privacy law, names and marks, encryption rules, consumer law, plain terms and a plan if the co-op stops. Accessibility law sits with accessibility (OS-A15-F8). Research only, not legal advice; each part needs a lawyer's check.

features.name: Get every part with its licence and source
features.does: See the licence and credit for every part of Spare OS, and get the source code for any part whose licence requires it.

parts.name: Licence inventory and software bill of materials
parts.what: A machine-readable list of every shipped part, its version, licence and origin, made by the build line in the same form as the kit's software bills of materials.

parts.name: Source archive for every release
parts.what: Keeps the exact source of every shipped part for each release for as long as the licences require.

parts.name: Licences screen
parts.what: Shows every part's licence and credit from the About page.

parts.name: Licence policy for shipped software
parts.what: Writes down, for an owner's decision, where our code ends and separate programs begin: our own libraries stay permissive, and for software that is not open source, such as NVIDIA's driver, device firmware files, the browser's streaming content protection module, game store apps and any Android store, which ship in the image, which are opt-in downloads the person chooses, and on what redistribution terms.

parts.name: Labels for software that is not open source
parts.what: Marks every driver, module or app that is not open source wherever it is offered, with its maker and terms, before the person chooses it.

features.name: Rely on Spare OS meeting product security law
features.does: Rely on Spare OS meeting product security law, such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act, whose reporting duties began in September 2026.

parts.name: Product security law research
parts.what: Whether the co-op is a manufacturer or an open-source steward of Spare OS under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, its distributor or importer duties for other makers' commercial apps sold into the EU through the store from 11 December 2027, and the duties for support periods, reporting and bills of materials; the research belongs in the kit for every Spare app.

parts.name: Reporting exploited flaws to authorities
parts.what: Reports actively exploited flaws and severe incidents to the right authority within the legal deadlines.

features.name: Meet age-assurance laws
features.does: Have the PC give apps only an age range where the law requires it, with nothing more shared.

parts.name: Age-assurance law research
parts.what: Tracks laws that put age duties on operating systems or app stores, such as California's from 1 January 2027 and Texas's app store law that courts let take effect in 2026, including parent consent for purchases, and designs the lightest way to comply.

parts.name: Age range service for apps
parts.what: A local service that tells permitted apps only the user's age range, never the birth date, and logs each request.

features.name: Handle app takedowns fairly
features.does: Know that harmful or unlawful apps are removed under published rules, with notice, appeal and a public log.

parts.name: Store rules and takedown process
parts.what: Published store rules, legal takedown handling and appeals, with every decision in the trust service's public log.

features.name: Have my data protected by law
features.does: Know Spare OS follows privacy law in NZ and overseas, including telling people about data breaches.

parts.name: Privacy law research
parts.what: Spare OS's duties under the NZ Privacy Act 2020, the EU's data protection law and others, worked through with the kit's privacy officer.

parts.name: Spare OS in the breach plan
parts.what: Adds Spare OS's own services, such as backups, sync, device finding and the store, to the kit's breach response.

features.name: Know the names and look are our own
features.does: Trust that Spare OS uses its own name, logo, icons and design, and names other companies only to say what it replaces.

parts.name: Name and look review
parts.what: Checks every release's names, icons and screens are our own work and not copies of another system.

parts.name: Name and logo registration
parts.what: Registers the Spare OS name and logo in the main markets; the registration work belongs in the kit for every Spare name.

features.name: Download Spare OS from any country
features.does: Download Spare OS legally from anywhere encryption export rules allow, knowing where local law limits encryption.

parts.name: Encryption export check
parts.what: Checks NZ and other export rules for publicly available encryption software, and laws in some countries that restrict importing or using encryption, which is on by default, and records the basis for shipping it; the research belongs in the kit for every Spare app.

features.name: Buy PCs and support with consumer rights
features.does: Have the usual consumer rights when buying a Spare OS PC or paid support.

parts.name: Consumer law research
parts.what: Spare OS's duties under NZ consumer and fair trading law, and overseas equivalents, for pre-installed PCs and paid support, building on the kit's consumer law research.

parts.name: Ecodesign rules for partner tablets
parts.what: Checks the EU ecodesign rules that require years of operating system updates for tablets, in case partners sell tablets with Spare OS.

features.name: Read terms I can understand
features.does: Read Spare OS's terms of use and the store's terms in plain words before agreeing.

parts.name: Spare OS terms of use
parts.what: Plain-words terms for Spare OS and its services, including the warranty disclaimer that free software licences carry, shown in the installer and on the website.

parts.name: Store terms for customers
parts.what: Plain-words terms for buying and installing apps from the store, including refunds and what the co-op checks.

features.name: Have the store, reviews and forum follow platform law
features.does: Know the store, its reviews and the forum handle notices, removals and complaints as platform law requires.

parts.name: EU Digital Services Act duties
parts.what: Notice and action, statements of reasons, complaints and, where it applies, checks on the makers selling apps, as the EU Digital Services Act requires of hosts and marketplaces.

parts.name: Harmful digital communications duties
parts.what: Handles complaints about reviews and forum posts under the NZ Harmful Digital Communications Act, so the co-op keeps its protection as a host.

parts.name: Copyright notices for member content
parts.what: Takes copyright notices for member-given wallpapers and forum posts through the kit's notice handling.

features.name: Know Spare OS carries on if the co-op stops
features.does: Know how updates, signing keys and mirrors would pass to another steward if the co-op or Spare OS stopped.

parts.name: Continuity plan
parts.what: A plan, held by the steward society, for handing the update service, signing keys and mirrors to another steward.

assess: Are the base system (OS01) and desktop (OS02) chosen on evidence, and which parts of this map change if the leans (KDE Plasma, image-based updates) change?
In the demo, can a Windows user find the start menu, files, settings and Wi-Fi in the first minute without help?
Is every icon, layout, sound and screen our own design, with nothing copied from Windows or any other system?
Can someone try Spare OS from a USB stick and go back to Windows untouched, and is BitLocker checked before any partition is changed?
Does the move from Windows bring files, browser data, email and Wi-Fi across without breaking any encryption or terms, and what happens to cloud-only files?
Of the 50 Windows programs NZ offices and schools use most, how many run, and is the compatibility list honest about the ones that don't?
Can an update ever leave a PC unable to start, and how is rollback tested on real hardware each release?
Who holds the signing keys and the Secure Boot signing agreement, and what is the plan if the firmware certificates change again?
Is every data-sharing choice off by default, and could a sceptical member check exactly what is sent?
Does every screen work with a screen reader and keyboard alone, and in te reo Māori?
Is the co-op a manufacturer or an open-source steward under EU product security law, and which duties (accessibility, age ranges, privacy, export) need a lawyer before the first release?
Is every system action a command, so scripts and AI use the same path as people, and can an AI only act with the person's approval?
What will Spare OS cost to run each month (build servers, mirrors, test lab, signing, support), and is it on the open cost ledger?
Is the core set small enough for a first release, or should more move to next?
Who helps people who get stuck, and can the member support network keep up if many people switch when old PCs lose Windows support?
Does any part depend on another Spare program directly, breaking the rule that programs depend only on the kit and engines?
For offices and schools, does the map replace directory and device-management licences fully, and which gaps are listed?
Are media patents, Microsoft fonts and streaming content protection handled legally, with the basis written down?

Which parts that are not open source (NVIDIA's driver, firmware files, streaming content protection, game stores, Android stores) ship in the image and which are opt-in, and has an owner signed that policy off against the README's legal rules?
Could a scammer use remote help on a first-time switcher, and what stops them: verified helpers, scope and time limits, the scam warning and the log?
Can a blind person unlock an encrypted Spare OS PC and finish install with no sighted help?
Who pays Spare OS's running costs when there are no jobs to charge a fee on, and have members voted on it?
Can NZ students sit NCEA digital exams on a Spare OS laptop, and can school PCs get online behind N4L's network?
